findings.title: Service's pods refuse the port it targets
findings.cause: container client exits because Service web refuses its connection on port 80, though the Service has ready pods: it forwards port 80 to the pods' port 80, and nothing in pod web-54b4cbcd4d-bts54 listens there, so the pod itself refuses. The pod counts as ready only because no readiness probe checks that port; the pod's command or env names port 8080, which is likely where the app listens; its log says: "wget: can't connect to remote host (10.96.110.109): Connection refused"; Deployment client has 0 of 1 replicas ready

evidence.what: container client exited with code 1 (Error), restarted 6 times
last lines of container client's log (run that exited)
evidence.detail:
Connecting to web (10.96.110.109:80)
wget: can't connect to remote host (10.96.110.109): Connection refused

evidence.what: Service web forwards port 80 to the pods' port 80
evidence.command: kubectl get service web -n kd-service-target-port-not-listening -o jsonpath='{range .spec.ports[*]}{.port}{" -> "}{.targetPort}{"\n"}{end}'

evidence.what: pod web-54b4cbcd4d-bts54 is Ready and behind Service web, and no readiness probe of it checks port 80
evidence.command: kubectl get pod web-54b4cbcd4d-bts54 -n kd-service-target-port-not-listening -o jsonpath='{range .spec.containers[*]}{.name}{" ports="}{.ports[*].containerPort}{" readiness="}{.readinessProbe}{" command="}{.command}{" "}{.args}{"\n"}{end}'

findings.fix: Set Service web's targetPort to 8080, the port the app listens on by its command or env (a containerPort in the pod spec is a label, not a setting: it does not make the app listen there), or make the app listen on 80 on all interfaces (0.0.0.0, not 127.0.0.1). Then add a readiness probe on that port, so a pod that does not answer gets no traffic and shows as not ready.
